pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme winds associated with Cyclone Gezani in February 2026.
pathways.documented_impact: Housing and service damage displaced people into temporary sites.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crowding and limited services in displacement sites weakened children's protective environment.
pathways.possible_consequence: UNICEF reports heightened risks of violence and exploitation, not measured post-cyclone incident rates.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequalities, household resources and service quality also influence protection risk.
Agency reporting is not an incident-based causal evaluation.
pathways.uncertainty: This is a source-stated post-disaster protection-risk mechanism, not proof of increased violence incidence, anthropogenic attribution of the cyclone, or a national FCV classification.
resilience_factors: Accessible shelters, privacy, lighting, sanitation and functioning protection referrals can address the reported risk factors; effectiveness is not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Post-Gezani displacement-site crowding and limited services heightened child violence/exploitation risk; incidence changes were not measured.

gaps: The panel summary supports source-stated livelihood-stress/violence mechanisms but not a causal effect estimate. Protection concerns after Gezani are not incident counts.
The humanitarian note attributes field-office closures to funding cuts; this is not evidence of conflict preventing a named climate intervention.
Protection pathway records a reported risk mechanism, not verified violence incidence or attribution of the cyclone to climate change.

executive_assessment.text: Southern Madagascar's panel evidence links drought-period livelihood stress with perceived violence and last-resort migration, subject to perception and attribution limits.
Named southern regions have reported restoration outputs; east-coast cyclone evidence adds differentiated service and protection vulnerabilities, with agency outputs distinguished from impact.
